overview.description: Doscientos ('Two Hundred') is a highly strategic partnership domino game widely played in Spain and Latin America. It is a straight-forward matching game where all 28 tiles of a double-six set are dealt, requiring teams to carefully track played suits and manage their remaining pips to win the round and reach the target score.

history.origins: Doscientos evolved from standard 19thndcentury Spanish domino rules. The name refers to the 200-point winning threshold typical in competitive matches throughout the Hispanic world.
timeline: 1800s: Dominoes gains massive popularity in Spain and later the Caribbean/Latin America.
Early 20th Century: Partnership variations become the standard for social club play.
Modern Era: Recognized by international domino federations as a fundamental tournament format.
history.evolution: The game shifted from individual play to fixed partnerships to emphasize communication (through play) and cooperative strategy.
history.cultural: Commonly played in plazas, social clubs, and at family gatherings across Latin America, particularly in Venezuela and Colombia.

setup.dealing: The set is shuffled face-down. Each player is dealt exactly 7 tiles.

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach a cumulative score of 200 points.
rules.gameplay:
1. Starting: In the first round, the holder of the 6-6 leads it. In subsequent rounds, the lead rotates.
2. Matching: Players take turns adding a tile to either end of the line, matching the pips on the open ends.
3. Passing: If a player cannot move, they must 'knock' (tap the table) and pass their turn.
4. Ending: The round ends when a player goes 'domino' (empties their hand) or the game is 'blocked' (no one can move).
keyRules: Anti-clockwise rotation is the standard for play.
Partners sit facing each other and are not allowed to show their tiles to one another.
A 'Trout' (closing the ends so no one can move) is a key strategic maneuver.

strategy.basic: Prioritize playing your 'strong suite' (the number you have the most of) to communicate your strength to your partner.
strategy.intermediate: If your partner leads a suit, try to 'keep it open' by matching the other end of the board to a different number, or play back to the same suit.
strategy.advanced: Counting: With only 28 tiles, you should track exactly how many of each suit (0-6) have been played. If your opponent has passed on a specific number, try to 'starve' them by keeping that number on the layout ends.
tips: Play your highndvalue doubles early to reduce your pip count in case the game is blocked.
If you hold the 6-6 and 6-5, leading the 6-6 is the standard 'opener' to signal your control of the 6s.

difficulty.medium: Tracks suit counts; avoids blocking the game if they have high pip counts.
difficulty.hard: Perfectly calculates the best move to 'starve' the opponent's known empty suits based on previous passes.

considerations: AI must support the shared partnership's goal of pip minimization.

engine.suitDescription: Domino tiles organized by pip combinations ranging from (0,0) blank to (6,6), where each combination represents a distinct tile value and contributes to the domino chain during gameplay.
engine.rankDescription: Domino tiles ranked by total pip count and combination type, where doubles (matching both sides) have special significance, and strategic placement along the chain determines game progression and scoring opportunities.
